label: First input token, when it is one of a b c g i j k l n o p q t u 2 3
explanation: Update-gate unit that fires at step 0 only, and only for a fixed subset of first tokens (a b c g i j k l n o p q t u 2 3). For those tokens it fires on every sequence (dev precision 1.0), and it never fires for the other first tokens (d e f h m r s v w x y z 0 1). At t=0 the activation depends only on the token. q is strongest (the top examples all start with q, about 18% of activation mass), then 2 and g. i, n and t are weak. The ~13% of activation mass it misses comes from small, sparse activations at t=1..3, mostly on the first occurrence of q, g, 2 or u in the sequence. Adding those raises recall but drops precision to about 0.70, so the F1 goes down. It essentially never fires at t>=4, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (6 activations out of about 64k).

issues: The t=0 part holds up. The predicate has test precision 1.0, recall 0.836 and F1 0.911. It never fires for the excluded first tokens (precision 0 at t==0 for tokens outside the set), and it is essentially silent at t>=4, on <DEL> and in the copy phase.

The claim that 'adding those raises recall but drops precision to about 0.70, so F1 goes down' is wrong. It only holds if you add every listed token at t=1..3 (precision about 0.07). Adding just the first occurrence of q at t=1..3 has precision 0.66 on dev on its own. Combined with the t=0 predicate it raises test F1 from 0.911 to 0.942 (precision 0.951, recall 0.933) and mass recall from 0.87 to 0.97.

The missed t=1..3 activations are called 'small, sparse', but the q misses are not small. Test misses include q at 0.46 and 0.28 of max, larger than most of the t=0 activations on weak tokens like i, n and t.

Systematic missed class: the first q in the sequence at steps 1 to 3. It fires in 66% of those cases overall, and in 98.5% when no token from the firing set came earlier. That makes it a real second mode, not scattered noise.

Small leftover: weaker misses on the first 2, g, j or l at steps 2 to 3, about 3% of activation mass. False positives of the improved predicate are mostly a q at step 1 to 3 after a strong t=0 token such as g or 3.
skeptic.revised_label: First input token when it is one of a b c g i j k l n o p q t u 2 3 (q strongest), plus the first q to appear at steps 1 to 3
